original.source: Every number computed in Step 1 is a coefficient in front of a local functional, and its sign and normalisation are inherited from three classical data: the odd pairing on the fields, the BV action and the linear differential $Q$. The sources supply the ten-dimensional action [ESW, (31)] and its dimensional reduction [ESW, Prop 2.20, §10.3], while the pairing on the antifields stays implicit in the phrase "natural $(-1)$-shifted symplectic structure" [ESW, Def 1.34]. This chapter fixes all three data for the reduction to Euclidean $\mathbb R^4$, writes the interaction vertex by vertex, and shows that the classical master equation determines the relative signs of the pairing.

For $w\in W_{\mathbb R}^\perp$, $w$ anticommutes with all four $v_i$, so $w\,(v_1v_2v_3v_4)=(+1)(v_1v_2v_3v_4)\,w$. Since $\rho(v)$ maps $\Sigma\to\Sigma^*$, the first relation reads $\rho(v)\rho(q(\mathrm{dvol}))|_{\Sigma}=-\rho(q(\mathrm{dvol}))|_{\Sigma^*}\rho(v)$, so $\rho(v)$ maps the $+1$ eigenspace on $\Sigma$ to the $-1$ eigenspace on $\Sigma^*$; the second relation gives $\rho(w)$ mapping the $+1$ eigenspace on $\Sigma$ to the $+1$ eigenspace on $\Sigma^*$. The dilatation of a composite operator, and every other superconformal transformation, acts on the fields of $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang–Mills theory up to gauge transformations and equations of motion. [ESW, (32)–(34), Thm 3.3] construct it for the Poincaré supersymmetry algebra; the special conformal transformations and the special supercharges require Weyl weights, a compensating term with the six scalars, and an R-symmetry rotation in the odd bracket.
